endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Audit rights: Reserve the right to audit vendor compliance with the DUA, including access logs, security practices, and data handling procedures.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Monitor third parties through audits to ensure they implement privacy and security controls required by contractual agreements.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Reserve the right to audit third-party vendors for compliance with the data use agreement and impose penalties for non-compliance.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Include clauses in contracts which allow an organization to evaluate third-party GAI processes and standards.

commentary.bottom_line: Four frameworks and guidance documents endorse reserving and exercising audit rights over AI vendors, two at the must level, but no supplied study tests whether audits detect or reduce vendor noncompliance. The recommendation rests on expert consensus rather than on measured effects.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests contractual audit rights or routine vendor audits, and no supplied study measures how often vendor noncompliance goes undetected. Under GRADE conventions, certainty about the practice's effect is rated as no direct evidence. The four endorsements agree on direction, but agreement among guidance documents does not substitute for outcome data.

Two CHAI documents frame audit rights as a must, and RUAIH and NIST AI 600-1 frame them as a should. The CHAI and RUAIH language centers on data use agreements and security controls. NIST extends it to evaluating third-party generative AI processes. None of the quoted passages cites a statute or regulation that requires such audits.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares organizations that audit AI vendors with those that do not on detected breaches of data use terms, security incidents, or performance drift. No study reports audit frequency, scope, or cost. Studies are needed that measure how often audits find noncompliance and whether findings lead to corrective action.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may have less bargaining power to negotiate audit clauses and fewer staff to conduct audits. Whether the practice is feasible or protective in those settings is unknown.
